prereg_text:
U5 pre-registration (written 2026-10-10 BEFORE any orbit run; not to be moved afterwards)

DESIGN CRITERION (design_synthesis.json, U5, unchanged):
  Engine pass iff ratio (C-A)/(B-A) = 0.0527 +/- 0.003, i.e. in [0.0497, 0.0557].
  Physics: sigma hook excluded iff Delta-omega_sigma = (C-A) > 0.05 arcsec/cy. Predicted ~2.3 arcsec/cy.
  Runs: 50 orbits, Forest-Ruth, dt = 600 s. A Newtonian; B include_gr=True; C Sun.sigma = XI*r_s/r updated every step.

ESTIMATOR (fixed before running):
  Primary  = direction of the osculating Laplace-Runge-Lenz vector (relative coords, mu = G(M_sun+M_mer), unscaled)
             evaluated at each discrete radial-minimum step; linear fit vs orbit index -> advance per orbit.
             Reason: the sketch's atan2(position) at the discrete minimum carries a timing term Omega_p*(t_sample - t_peri)
             that does not cancel in C-A once the anomalistic period changes (estimated ~1e-7 rad/orbit vs signal 2.6e-8).
  Secondary (reported, not used for pass/fail) = the sketch's own estimator verbatim, and parabola-interpolated
             position angle at the r minimum.

ADDED PREDICTIONS FROM READING THE CODE (made before running):
  P1  nbody.py gr_1pn branch (lines ~463-477) adds +factor*[(4GM/r - v^2) r_hat + 4 (r_hat.v) v] with r_hat pointing
      FROM Mercury TO the Sun. The standard harmonic-gauge 1PN test-body EOM is +(GM/c^2 r^3)[(4GM/r - v^2) x + 4 (x.v) v]
      with x pointing from the Sun to Mercury. The engine term is the overall NEGATIVE of the standard one.
      => predicted B-A = -1.00 x Delta-omega_GR (retrograde, about -43 arcsec/cy), so the design ratio (C-A)/(B-A) comes
      out about -0.0527 and the design's engine criterion FAILS on the GR run's sign, not on the sigma hook.
      Force-level probe: cos(angle) between engine a_1PN and the standard a_1PN at perihelion predicted = -1.
  Corrected criterion (reported alongside the original): (C-A)/Delta-omega_GR,analytic in [0.0497, 0.0557], with
      Delta-omega_GR,analytic = 6 pi G M /(c^2 a (1-e^2)) evaluated by Mentat simplify_expr; and |B-A|/Delta-omega_GR,analytic
      in [0.99, 1.01] with its sign recorded.
  P2  add-on run D, sigma = sigma_from_potential(r, M_sun) = XI*r_s/(2r) (the inventory normalisation):
      (D-A)/Delta-omega_GR,analytic = XI/6 = 0.02637 +/- 0.0015.
  P3  add-on run E, toggles eih_cross=True: radial terms carry the standard sign, the velocity cross term
      (vec_ij.(4v_i-3v_j))(v_i-v_j) carries the opposite sign of Moyer/Will (they use x_i - x_j). Coefficient bookkeeping
      Delta-omega = (pi m/p)(-A_coef - 2 B_coef + 2 D_coef) with A=4, B=-1, D=-4 gives -10 pi m/p = -(5/3) Delta-omega_GR.
      Predicted (E-A)/Delta-omega_GR,analytic = -1.667 +/- 0.03.
  P4  dt-halving control (A and C at dt = 300 s): (C-A) changes by < 1 %.

engine_defects.defect: gr_1pn branch has the overall wrong sign: adds +GM/(r^2 c^2)[(4GM/r - v^2) r_hat + 4 (r_hat.v) v] with r_hat = (x_source - x_body)/r, i.e. the negative of IERS Conventions eq. 10.12 (r from central body to satellite).
engine_defects.evidence: force probe at perihelion: cos(engine, IERS 10.12) = -1.0, |ratio| = 1.0000000000; 50-orbit run: (B-A) = -42.991 arcsec/cy = -1.0000035 x 6 pi GM/(c^2 a(1-e^2)); predicted from code reading before the run. The suite's test_mercury_precesses_with_gr_on (test_physics_stability.py:215) only asserts a non-zero position difference, so it cannot see the sign.

engine_defects.defect: eih_cross branch: velocity cross term (vec_ij.(4v_i-3v_j))(v_i-v_j) uses vec_ij = x_j - x_i where the EIH/Moyer form uses x_i - x_j; the radial A_ij terms (line 455) carry the correct sign.
engine_defects.evidence: 50-orbit run E: (E-A) = -71.652 arcsec/cy = -1.6666675 x GR, matching the pre-registered coefficient bookkeeping (pi m/p)(-A - 2B + 2D) with D = -4 instead of +4, i.e. -5/3 x GR to 5e-7. Correct EIH would give +1 x GR.

design_corrections: The design's engine criterion compares C-A with the engine's own GR run B-A. B-A is retrograde (-1.000 x GR) because of the sign defect, so the design ratio is -0.0527 and the criterion fails for a reason unrelated to the sigma hook. Corrected criterion: (C-A) against the analytic GR advance 6 pi GM/(c^2 a(1-e^2)) evaluated by Mentat: 0.0527335 -> PASS.

The design sketch's perihelion estimator (atan2 of the position one step after the discrete radial minimum) has sampling jitter of 2.2e-4 rad rms per orbit, four orders above the sigma signal (2.6e-8 rad/orbit); it returns a ratio of 0.171 and C/GR = -1.56, i.e. noise. Primary estimator fixed before running: osculating Laplace-Runge-Lenz direction at the radial minimum (residual rms 1e-11 rad); parabola-interpolated angle agrees to 3e-7 relative.

Normalisation: the repo has two sigma amplitudes for the same body. Field-equation sigma = xi r_s/r gives xi/3 = 0.0527 (2.27 arcsec/cy); inventory sigma_from_potential = xi r_s/(2r) gives xi/6 = 0.0264 (1.13 arcsec/cy). Both excluded (45x and 23x the 0.05 arcsec/cy budget).
The 0.05 arcsec/cy threshold (~1e-3 of GR, Will 2014 Living Rev.) is conservative; Park+2017's beta-1 = (-2.7 +/- 3.9)e-5 makes the hook (an effective PPN beta shift of -xi) ~4e3 sigma out.
coupling_convention_record: nbody.CelestialBody.gm_m3_s2 (nbody.py:225-233) multiplies the SOURCE body's whole GM by e^sigma; with sigma set from the test body's distance this is a universal, attractive 1/r^3 addition. inventory.core.sigma.proton_mass_kg scales only the QCD part (929.25/938.27 = 0.99) of the TEST body's mass, which as a field gradient force -grad(m c^2) is repulsive (program section 14, U1). sigma_from_potential uses xi GM/(r c^2) = xi r_s/2r; the field equation gives xi r_s/r. Three conventions, two amplitudes.
